scenes.sub: AWT asks the operating system to draw buttons. It is heavy and looks different on each OS.
Swing draws its own buttons in pure Java. It is light and looks the same everywhere.
You can change the whole style (Metal, Nimbus, Windows) with one line.
JButton, JLabel, JTextField, JFrame… all in javax.swing.
Data (model) is kept apart from the view, so components are flexible.
AWT is heavy (uses OS), Swing is light (pure Java).

steps.say: All Swing classes live in the package javax.swing.
A JFrame (the window) is made in memory.
A JButton is made. Note the J at the start: it is a Swing component.
The button is put inside the window.
Size is set and the window appears.

answer_html:
Definition

Swing is a Java GUI toolkit (package javax.swing) used to build windows, buttons, text boxes and other graphical parts. It is built on top of AWT and is written fully in Java.

Features of Swing

  • Lightweight: components are drawn by Java, not by the operating system.
  • Pluggable look and feel: the style can be changed at run time.
  • MVC based: data (model) is separate from display (view).
  • Platform independent: looks the same on all OS.
  • Rich components: JTable, JTree, JTabbedPane, etc. (names start with J).
